title: Scalar extension compares all Proj twists with their normalized fraction maps
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ be a commutative unital graded ring with a ring map $R\to A_0$. Grade $S\otimes_RA$ by $(S\otimes_RA)_n=S\otimes_RA_n$. Let $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}B_n$ be a commutative unital graded ring with an $S$-algebra structure whose unit map $S\to B$ has image in $B_0$, let $\beta:S\otimes_RA\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ be a graded $S$-algebra isomorphism (for instance $B=S\otimes_RA$ and $\beta=\mathrm{id}$), and put $\psi(a)=\beta(1\otimes a)$. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ and $Q=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$, and let $r=r_\psi:Q\to P$ be the scalar-extension morphism of [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension]. Use the twisting modules $\mathcal O_P(j)=\widetilde{A(j)}$ and $\mathcal O_Q(j)=\widetilde{B(j)}$, their homogeneous sections, and their localized fractions from [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. For every $j\in\mathbf Z$ there is a canonical isomorphism of module sheaves
$$\theta^\psi_j:r^*\mathcal O_P(j)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_Q(j)$$
[def-pc-module-pullback]. Its restriction to $D_+(\psi(f))$ for every $f\in A_d$, $d>0$, is the sheaf map associated to the isomorphism
$$(A_f)_j\otimes_{(A_f)_0}(B_{\psi(f)})_0\xrightarrow{\sim}(B_{\psi(f)})_j,\qquad (a/f^m)\otimes c\longmapsto c\,\psi(a)/\psi(f)^m,$$
where $m\geq0$ and $a\in A_{md+j}$, with $A_i=0$ for $i<0$. These maps commute with further restrictions of standard opens. They preserve the units and multiplication maps of the twisting modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], whose fraction formula is $(a/f^m)\otimes(b/f^n)\mapsto ab/f^{m+n}$; in degree zero $\theta^\psi_0$ is the structural identification $r^*\mathcal O_P\cong\mathcal O_Q$. For $j\geq0$ and $a\in A_j$, $\theta^\psi_j$ carries the pullback of the homogeneous section $a/1$ to $\psi(a)/1$. Composition: let $S\to T$ be a further ring homomorphism, $C=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}C_n$ a commutative unital graded ring with a $T$-algebra structure whose unit map has image in $C_0$, $\gamma:T\otimes_SB\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ a graded $T$-algebra isomorphism, and $\chi(b)=\gamma(1\otimes b)$. Then $\gamma\circ(\mathrm{id}_T\otimes\beta)$, precomposed with the canonical isomorphism $T\otimes_RA\cong T\otimes_S(S\otimes_RA)$, is a graded $T$-algebra isomorphism $T\otimes_RA\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ with associated map $\chi\circ\psi$; one has $r_{\chi\circ\psi}=r_\psi\circ r_\chi$, and after the canonical pullback-composition isomorphism $(r_\psi\circ r_\chi)^*\cong r_\chi^*r_\psi^*$ one has $\theta^{\chi\circ\psi}_j=\theta^\chi_j\circ r_\chi^*\theta^\psi_j$ for every $j$. For $R=S$, $B=A$ and $\beta$ the multiplication isomorphism $R\otimes_RA\cong A$, the comparison is the identity. No flatness, finite generation, equality $A_0=R$, or non-zero-divisor hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put $V_f=D_+(f)$ and $U_f=D_+(\psi(f))$. The scalar-extension Proj lemma gives $r^{-1}V_f=U_f$, their affine chart ring map, and the covering $Q=\bigcup_fU_f$. The twists are quasi-coherent: apply the graded-module sheaf existence theorem (c) to $A(j)$ and $B(j)$. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence. Consequently the affine pullback-sections theorem identifies $\Gamma(U_f,r^*\mathcal O_P(j))$ with $(A_f)_j\otimes_{(A_f)_0}(B_{\psi(f)})_0$, by $(a/f^m)\otimes c\mapsto c\,r^*(a/f^m)$. Its hypotheses hold because both $V_f$ and $U_f$ are affine, $U_f\subseteq r^{-1}V_f$, and $\mathcal O_P(j)$ is quasi-coherent. This applies to every integer $j$, with no assertion that the twist is invertible.

proof.text:
Write $H=(A_f)_0$ and $L_j=(A_f)_j$. The degree-zero localization comparison, followed by $\beta$ on fractions, identifies $(B_{\psi(f)})_0$ with $S\otimes_RH$. There is an explicit isomorphism $L_j\otimes_H(S\otimes_RH)\cong S\otimes_RL_j$: send $u\otimes(s\otimes h)$ to $s\otimes hu$, with inverse $s\otimes u\mapsto u\otimes(s\otimes1)$. These formulas respect the $R$- and $H$-balancing relations and their composites are identities on pure tensors. Apply the homogeneous-module localization comparison to $M=A$ and degree $j$, and then the map on localized modules induced by the graded isomorphism $\beta$. The resulting isomorphism
$$F_{f,j}:L_j\otimes_H(B_{\psi(f)})_0\xrightarrow{\sim}(B_{\psi(f)})_j$$
is exactly $(a/f^m)\otimes c\mapsto c\psi(a)/\psi(f)^m$: first check $c=\beta_f(s\otimes h)$, then use additivity. The extension from pure tensors uses only the balanced tensor relations.

proof.text: On the affine scheme $U_f$, both sheaves in question are quasi-coherent by step 1. The affine tilde--global-sections adjunction, with its isomorphic counit for quasi-coherent modules, therefore turns $F_{f,j}$ into a unique sheaf isomorphism $\theta_{f,j}$. Its inverse is obtained from $F_{f,j}^{-1}$ by the same functor. This supplies the sheaf maps as well as their inverses, rather than just an abstract bijection of section modules.

source.place: Tags 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions), 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine), 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent); application to the local maps of constructions.tex 01MY.

proof.text: The local maps agree on overlaps. On $U_{fg}=U_f\cap U_g$, a section $a/f^m$ restricts to $ag^m/(fg)^m$; applying either local formula gives $\psi(a)\psi(g)^m/\psi(fg)^m$. For the map from the $g$-chart the identical argument uses $bf^n/(fg)^n$. These checks determine the maps on the entire overlap: by the affine pullback-sections theorem the pullbacks of sections on $V_f$, together with coefficients on $U_{fg}$, generate the source there. Equality on global sections determines maps between these quasi-coherent sheaves on the affine overlap by the affine adjunction. More generally, for $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$ choose $g^e=hf$ as in the graded-module sheaf theorem (a). Restriction sends $a/f^m$ to $h^ma/g^{em}$, and both orders of restriction and comparison send it to $\psi(h)^m\psi(a)/\psi(g)^{em}$; coefficients restrict by the ring map. Thus all specified standard-open restrictions commute. Glue the $\theta_{f,j}$ by the module-sheaf gluing theorem (1). Their inverses agree as well, since they are inverses to equal maps on overlaps, so gluing them gives the inverse of the resulting canonical $\theta_j^\psi$.

source.place: Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), final paragraph of proof; Tag 01M7 (lemma-proj-sheaves), restrictions. Sheaves Tag 04TN (lemma-glue-maps), applied to modules.

proof.text: Multiplication is respected on each $U_f$: on two pure tensors $(a/f^m)\otimes c$ and $(b/f^n)\otimes e$, the two orders of comparison and multiplication both give $ce\,\psi(ab)/\psi(f)^{m+n}$. Balancing and additivity extend this to all tensors. The affine quasi-coherent tensor-sections theorem identifies these tensor modules with the section modules of the sheaf tensor products. The canonical pullback--tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] sends $r^*(u\otimes v)$ to $r^*u\otimes r^*v$; on the chart it is therefore precisely the rebracketing $(u\otimes c)\otimes(v\otimes e)\mapsto(u\otimes v)\otimes ce$; its inverse sends $(u\otimes v)\otimes c$ to $(u\otimes1)\otimes(v\otimes c)$, so the comparison in this diagram is the canonical one. The local product formulas also define the twist multiplication maps, since multiplication of graded fractions commutes with restrictions. The unit is $1/1$, sent to $1/1$; at $j=0$ the formula $h\otimes c\mapsto c\psi(h)$ is exactly the structural identification $r^*\mathcal O_P\cong\mathcal O_Q$. Finally for $a\in A_j$, $j\geq0$, its canonical global section restricts to $a/1$, which the local formula sends to $\psi(a)/1$. Gluing uniqueness proves these identities globally.

source.place: Tag 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj), proof on standard opens; Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), normalized fractions; Tag 01MZ (lemma-morphism-proj-transitive).

proof.text: For $S\to T$ and $\gamma$ as in the statement, the tensor associator sends $t\otimes a$ to $t\otimes(1\otimes a)$; its inverse sends $t\otimes(s\otimes a)$ to $ts\otimes a$. Balancing verifies these are inverse graded $T$-algebra maps. Composing with $\gamma(\mathrm{id}\otimes\beta)$ therefore gives the asserted graded isomorphism and map $a\mapsto\chi\psi(a)$. The inverse image under $r_\psi r_\chi$ of $D_+(f)$ is $D_+(\chi\psi(f))$; both scheme morphisms there have fraction map $a/f^m\mapsto\chi\psi(a)/\chi\psi(f)^m$. Uniqueness in the scalar-extension Proj lemma proves $r_{\chi\psi}=r_\psi r_\chi$. On this covering of $\operatorname{Proj}(C)$, affine pullback computes the iterated pullback by triple tensors. The canonical pullback-composition isomorphism sends $((u\otimes b)\otimes c)$ to $u\otimes\chi(b)c$. Both candidate twist comparisons consequently send $((a/f^m)\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $c\chi(b)\chi\psi(a)/\chi\psi(f)^m$. Pure tensors generate, and affine adjunction and gluing uniqueness give the composition equation for every $j$. For the identity coefficient extension, the Proj chart maps are identities, hence $r=\mathrm{id}$ by the same uniqueness. The twist chart formula becomes $u\otimes c\mapsto cu$, the canonical identity-pullback identification; gluing gives the claimed identity comparison.
